title: Theologians’ preached certainty is objective, not every subject’s actual grade
source_text: XIX. Verum, quum tanta praedicatur a Theologis fidei certitudo, priore modo illam considerant, & rationem habent, non ejus certitudinis, quam actu in mente hujus aut illius obtinet, quae subjectiva dici potest: sed ejus quam sibi ex se, & natura sua vendicat, sive quam objectum fidei jure suo a mente postulat, quae idcirco certitudo objectiva dicenda est.
pass_a_gloss: But when so great a certainty of faith is preached by the Theologians, they consider it in the former way, and have regard not to that certainty which it actually obtains in this or that mind — which can be called subjective — but to that which it claims for itself from itself and by its nature, or which the object of faith by its own right demands from the mind, which therefore is to be called objective certainty.
pass_b_english: Not subjective grade actually in this/that mind.
Objective: what faith/object by nature demands from the mind.

choices.term: quae idcirco certitudo objectiva dicenda est
choices.english: which therefore is to be called objective certainty
choices.why: Reuses II’s split for faith’s preached summit.
rejected: theologians mean each believer’s actual feeling-grade
